*   **Strengths:** Produces better image quality than splatting (no splatting artifacts) [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the technique produces better image quality than splatting with no splatting artifacts. Source [S1] explicitly states in section 2.2: 'Compared to the splatting technique, the advantage of direct volume ray casting is that it produces a better image quality (as there are no splatting artifacts, see Figure 3).' This directly supports every part of the claim.

*   **When to use:** When image quality is prioritized over interactive performance and splatting artifacts are unacceptable [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that volume ray casting 'produces a better image quality (as there are no splatting artifacts)' compared to splatting. It also notes that the technique is 'more computationally intensive' and that the software implementation is 'not interactive on a large dataset'. Therefore, the claim that it should be used when image quality is prioritized over interactive performance and splatting artifacts are unacceptable is fully supported by the text.

*   **Performance:** The software implementation is not interactive on large datasets (e.g., Milky Way simulation with ~200 million AMR cells) [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the software implementation is not interactive on large datasets, specifically citing the Milky Way simulation with ~200 million AMR cells. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'On the other hand this technique is more computationally intensive, which means our software implementation is not interactive on a large dataset like our Milky Way simulation.' Additionally, the caption for Figure 3 confirms the Milky Way simulation has 'around 200 million of AMR cells.' Therefore, every fact in the claim is present and supported by the evidence.
supported

Adaptive Volume Ray Casting is a volume rendering technique where one ray is shot through the volume for each pixel, traversing an octree to accumulate physical values along the ray path [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that Adaptive Volume Ray Casting is a volume rendering technique where one ray is shot through the volume for each pixel, traversing an octree to accumulate physical values along the ray path. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in section 2.2: 'For each pixel of the image, one ray is shot through our volume... The algorithm starts from the root and then goes down the octree... The cell physical value observed is then multiplied by the length... Every contribution along the ray is then added to the resulting pixel value'. The term 'Adaptive' is supported by the context of the document which discusses 'adaptive ray tracing' and adaptive resolution handling (octree traversal based on camera resolution). All specific facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
supported
